scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service subscription canceled 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Brad Miller and I'm 27. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Brad, I understand you're looking for a refund on your subscription. I can certainly look into your account for you. To get started, could you please provide the email address associated with your account and the last four digits of the credit card used for the transaction?
Sure, the email is brad.miller@email.com and the card ends in 4492.
Thanks for that. And just to confirm, could you please verify your full billing address on file?
Yes, it's 123 Maple Street, Springfield, IL 62704.

Thank you, Brad. I see the account here. Per our standard Terms of Service, section 4.2, refund requests must be submitted within 30 days of the charge date. Since you are at 34 days, I am technically outside of my authority to process this automatically.
I understand the policy, but like I said, I was traveling and the charge was unexpected. Is there really no way to make an exception?

I hear you. I'll go ahead and escalate this to our billing supervisor for a manual review. They have the ability to override the 30-day limit in cases of extenuating circumstances. I've logged your request and the reason for the delay.

escalation_reason: The request falls outside the standard 30-day refund window defined in section 4.2 of the Terms of Service, requiring supervisor approval for an exception.

judge_scores.justification: The agent conducted appropriate verification and accurately cited section 4.2 of the Terms of Service to explain the 30-day limit. Because the request exceeded their authority, they efficiently and appropriately escalated the case to a supervisor while acknowledging the customer's extenuating circumstances.
